short_answers.q: Why is the subject biology named as a multidimensional subject?
short_answers.answer: Biology is linked with other sciences such as physics, chemistry and mathematics. For example, the movement of animals follows the laws of motion in physics. Because it is related to many sciences, it is called a multidimensional, interdisciplinary science.

short_answers.q: How does the farming profession help mankind?
short_answers.answer: Different kinds of farms are developed, such as fish farms, cattle farms and poultry farms. New technologies are used to produce animals as sources of meat, milk, leather and wool.

short_answers.q: Why is species called the smallest taxonomic level?
short_answers.answer: Species is the smallest unit of taxonomic organization. It includes morphologically similar living organisms which inter-breed and produce fertile offspring.

short_answers.q: How is population different from community?
short_answers.answer: A population consists of all members of one species living in a specific habitat. A community consists of members of different species living in a specific habitat.

short_answers.q: How are new varieties of plants produced?
short_answers.answer: Through horticulture, in which work is carried out for the development of new varieties of plants and their products. Biotechnology deals with manipulation of genes to achieve desirable characters.

long_answers.q: Describe the role of Muslim scientists in the field of biology.
long_answers.answer:
Muslim scientists played a great role in the development of biological science. The textbook states that they began experiments and observations from the first century of Hijra.

1. Jabir Bin Hayan (722–817 A.D.): Born in Iran. He worked in chemistry and also wrote books on plants and animals, including Al-Nabatiat and Al-Haywan.
2. Abdul Malik Asmai (741–828 A.D.): A great zoologist who wrote books on animals, including Al-Kheil on horses, Al-Ibil on camels, Al-Shat on sheep, Al-Wahoosh on wild animals and Khalqul Insan on parts of the human body and their functions.
3. Bu Ali Sina (980–1037 A.D.): Considered the founder of medicine and called Avicenna in the West. He identified diseases including tuberculosis and meningitis and wrote Al-Qanoon and Fil Tib Al-Shafa.

long_answers.q: Describe the relationships of biology to other sciences.
long_answers.answer:
Biology is a multidimensional, interdisciplinary science.

1. Biophysics: Laws and techniques of physics are applied to explain processes of life. Radioactive isotopes, radio-labeling, carbon-dating, ultrasound and laser technology are examples.
2. Biomathematics/Biometry: The branch of mathematics which collects data of living organisms and plays an important role in research.
3. Biochemistry: Study of molecules that form living organisms or cells, requiring knowledge of biology and chemistry.
4. Biogeography: Deals with distribution of living organisms in different geographical regions.
5. Bio-economics: Deals with economically important organisms involved in production, with cost and profit values considered.

The levels of organization in the living world are based on chemical foundation.

1. Atomic level: Matter is made of elements composed of atoms. Sixteen elements are bio-elements and are vital for life; C, H, O, N, S and P are the six basic elements of life.
2. Molecular level: Atoms bind to form bio-molecules, classified as micro-molecules and macro-molecules.
3. Cellular level: Biomolecules form protoplasm; when protoplasm works as a unit it is called a cell. Similar cells form tissues, tissues form organs, organs form organ systems, and organ systems form a multicellular organism.
4. Taxonomic level: Species is the smallest unit of taxonomic organization and includes morphologically similar organisms that inter-breed and produce fertile offspring.
5. Population level: All members of a species living in a specific habitat.
6. Community level: Members of different species living in a specific habitat.
7. Ecological system: Communities interact with their non-living environment; this interaction is called an ecosystem.
8. Biosphere level: The part of earth where life exists; it consists of different kinds of ecosystems.
